To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) speaker recognition performance is significantly affected by the type of speech (spontaneous vs. read), the type of task (speaker verification vs. identification), and the type of system (text-independent vs. dependent).

(a) the use of a single speaker model for verification is a viable approach for large vocabulary verification systems, (b) the use of speaker specific models can improve verification performance, and (c) a speaker verification system can be made robust to channel mismatch by using a single speaker model and training on multiple channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing algorithms to improve the performance of large vocabulary continuous speech recognition systems.
developing techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of automatic speech recognition.
